Yes, in the v2 snapshot `Executor.map` accepts `buffersize`, and its default is `None`.

```json
{"facts": {"available": "true", "default": "None"}}
```

The signature in `library/concurrent.futures.rst` is `map(fn, *iterables, timeout=None, chunksize=1, buffersize=None)`. By default the iterables are collected immediately. If you set a `buffersize`, it caps how many submitted tasks can have results not yet yielded. When the buffer is full, iteration over the iterables pauses until a result is yielded.

An earlier conversation in my context search concluded the parameter was unavailable. That result contradicts this corpus, so I did not rely on it.
